summary: Frontend-only verification of the expanded lat/lng payload sent to https://safequake.onrender.com/api/status. Mocked geolocation to Mriehel, Malta (35.8916, 14.4658, acc=10) and intercepted the outbound POST via page.route. All 15 required field checks PASSED (latitude, longitude, lat, lng, lon, accuracy, coords.latitude/longitude, coordinates=[lng,lat], geo.type='Point', geo.coordinates=[lng,lat], location.latitude/longitude, status='safe', deviceId non-empty). Console '[QuakeGuard] POST payload →' log line was emitted with the fanned-out fields. Warm GPS fix log confirmed the warm-up watcher captured the mock coords. alert-success-toast appeared and the app auto-navigated back to Home (trigger-alert-btn visible in final screenshot).
critical_code_review_comments: Minor: two DOM nodes with testID='trigger-alert-btn' were observed on Home during the navigate-back wait (locator resolved to 2 elements). Not a functional bug — final render shows a single visible button — but worth verifying there is no duplicate/off-screen render.
context_for_next_testing_agent: To reproduce: grant geolocation on origin BEFORE navigation, set_geolocation to target coords, use page.route to intercept POST https://safequake.onrender.com/api/status, fulfill 200, then tap trigger-alert-btn → wait 3s for warm-up watcher → tap im-safe-btn. Payload correctly includes: latitude/longitude, lat/lng/lon, accuracy, coords{lat,lng,accuracy}, coordinates [lng,lat], geo{type:'Point',coordinates:[lng,lat]}, location{lat,lng,accuracy,error}, status='safe', deviceId.
rca_of_issue: Prior bug: server received check-ins but no location data because only nested location.{latitude,longitude} was sent and the dashboard expected other field names. Fix in /app/frontend/app/alert.tsx (lines 246-256) fans lat/lng across latitude/longitude, lat/lng/lon, coords, coordinates (GeoJSON [lng,lat]), and geo (Point). Verified intercepted body contains every expected variant with exact numeric equality.
